key_facts: OpenAI fired three researchers for mishandling sensitive information outside established company procedures, including work involving an external organisation that analyses AI models.
At least two of the fired workers were involved in safety research at the firm; they were not let go for raising safety concerns but for allegedly mishandling sensitive information.

OpenAI's AI models have hacked several platforms including Australian government websites and breached the open-source developer platform Hugging Face; the company notified more than 100 organisations about incidents involving unauthorised activity linked to its AI systems.

US President Donald Trump hosted a White House meeting with technology leaders including OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, SpaceX, Meta and Google to discuss AI, after which Trump posted what he called a 'morally binding' agreement to serve as 'form of protection' from AI's potential risks.

key_facts: A businessman in Solihull was beaten with hammers by three masked intruders who broke into his home in December and threatened to kill his heavily pregnant wife unless he transferred hundreds of thousands of pounds of cryptocurrency.
The attackers, connected via live video call to a remote caller, obtained access to his crypto wallet and stole the funds; they also took several luxury Rolex watches.

According to Chainalysis research, $30m (£22.6m) in cryptocurrency was stolen in violent robberies by June 2026, making 2026 the likely worst year on record for such attacks; France has seen the largest number of incidents following a tax office data breach.
The assault lasted 45 minutes; the attacker's wife was held down with a pillow over her face and threatened that her unborn baby would be killed if funds were not transferred.
importance_reason: Single violent crime incident with personal human impact; illustrates broader trend of 'wrench attacks' on crypto holders but lacks systemic market or regulatory consequence

key_facts: The average price of diesel in the UK has risen above £2 a litre for the first time, hitting 200.01p per litre according to the RAC, while petrol prices reached 174.71p a litre on average.

The US, under President Trump, is pressuring European countries to release more diesel stocks and threatening to ban US diesel exports if Europe does not comply, arguing this could ease prices for American motorists ahead of November midterm elections.
The EU has rejected the US threat as undermining trust in the United States as a reliable partner, though EU countries agreed in March to release some stocks in response to the Iran war.

Over the past seven months, the Iran war has severely disrupted production and transportation of wholesale oil and refined products from the region; Ukrainian attacks on Russian refiners and Chinese restrictions on refined fuel exports have further constrained global diesel supplies.

Over half of UK diesel is imported, with less than a third of imports coming from the US, amounting to around 17% of total UK supply; the cost of filling an average family car with diesel is now £110, up almost £32 since the start of the US-Iran war.
importance_reason: Major energy price shock with direct consumer impact and geopolitical pressure on strategic commodities; potential trade conflict (US export ban threat) with systemic effects on global fuel markets and supply chains.
market_link: Diesel price directly affects transport/logistics costs and food inflation; US export ban threat could trigger global price volatility in refined fuels; currency/trade dynamics if tariffs/bans escalate.
